reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify potential spurious features through cross-instance pattern analysis with XAI tools to quantitatively validate feature importance and detect shared attribution across misclassified instances. This ensures both pattern recognition and statistical reliability in identifying features that are semantically irrelevant yet influential in misclassification.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the feature values of instances 541 and 291 to identify shared numerical patterns in the input features, particularly in low-impact or numerically similar values across the dataset.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that have identical or highly similar values across both misclassified instances (e.g., mean smoothness ≈ 0.089, mean compactness ≈ 0.10).

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features lack semantic relevance to cancer classification (e.g., concavity, concave points, smoothness) based on domain knowledge and typical cancer biomarkers.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification of why specific shared features are not semantically aligned with the target class (malignant/unknown).

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a global understanding of feature importance across all instances, identifying which features consistently have high influence in misclassified cases. Integrated Gradients offer an interpretable gradient-based attribution pathway, especially helpful in detecting spurious features that dominate prediction in the absence of strong semantic relevance. Sensitivity analysis isolates the contribution of each feature by perturbing it, confirming whether its removal leads to meaningful changes in prediction outcomes, thus validating spuriousness.
